edge.title: Meter politics at the junction
edge.anchor: Heavy rain snarled Bengaluru traffic on 15 October and ride-hailing fares surged (The Hindu).
edge.setup: Auto refuses the meter and quotes a flat fare, double. It's raining, you're late, there's no other auto, and he knows all three. This is not fraud — it's a negotiation where he currently holds every card.
edge.tell: If you're arguing about the price, you've already accepted that he's the only option.
move: Change where you stand. Walk 100m to the main road; scarcity was the only leverage he had.
Open an app and let him watch. The visible alternative resets the price more reliably than argument.
If you need the formal route: the refusal, auto number and location go to the Bengaluru Traffic Police app or 080-22868550. Mentioning you're noting the number often ends the matter.
Never start with anger. Start with the alternative — anger is a worse tool than a visible option.
edge.why: Price is set by alternatives, not by fairness. Every effective move here manufactures an alternative — distance, an app, a complaint channel — rather than appealing to rules. This is the whole of negotiation in miniature.
edge.variants: Same shape: surge pricing you can wait out, 'last room available' at a hotel desk, the mechanic who found three more problems.

lens.name: Goodhart's Law
lens.one_line: When a measure becomes a target, it stops measuring what it used to.
lens.detail: Any number used to judge people will be optimised directly, often by routes that bypass the thing the number was standing in for. Not usually by cheating — by honest, rational effort aimed at the metric rather than the goal, because the metric is what's rewarded.
elsewhere: Police judged on cases closed may book easier cases and discourage hard complaints.
Schools judged on pass rates quietly move weak students out before the exam.
Support teams judged on ticket-closing time close tickets fast, unresolved.
lens.test: What number are these people judged on, and what's the cheapest way to move it that doesn't involve doing the actual job?
lens.today: Officials in Bengaluru South have been told to act within 10 days on 1,000 garbage spots flagged by AI (The Hindu). Once 'spots cleared' is the number, the cheapest way to hit it is to clear the same spots repeatedly, not to stop the dumping. Watch whether a cleared spot near you stays clear a month later.

carry_over.prompt: A small loan app approved in minutes starts calling your contacts, your manager and your family after one missed payment. What is that pressure actually aimed at?
carry_over.answer: The pressure is aimed at your reputation, not your bank account — which means it's outside the law, not inside it.
